messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — launching a new prepaid "pool" option + burst-credit smoothing next week. Details below.

maya: Why: customers asked for predictable unit economics without committing to Dedicated. Prepaid pools let teams pre-fund a shared credits bucket and draw down per-request. Burst smoothing prevents sharp overage spikes during traffic bursts. :sparkles:

patrick: Finance note: prepay pools are billed immediately when created. We apply a 7-day rolling smoothing window to overage charges for any route tied to a pool. This reduces surprise invoices for bursty customers.

devin: TL;DR on mechanics: each pool has a balance (USD). Requests charge against the pool. If pool exhausted, requests fall back to standard metered billing (or a configured fallback model).

lisa: Sizing guidance: recommend prepay = 2x expected weekly spend for bursty workloads. We’ll ship a calculator in Console.

maya: How to opt-in: Console -> Billing -> Pools -> Create pool, or use our CLI. Example: 
```
# create a pool named "mobile-burst" with $5k prepay
redwood billing create-pool --name mobile-burst --currency USD --amount 5000 --region us-west-2
```

maya: Link to docs: <https://redwood.internal/docs/billing/prepay-pools|Prepaid pools & burst smoothing> (internal).

patrick: Overage smoothing specifics: we’ll amortize any spike over the 7-day window when computing invoices. That means if a route spikes on day 1 and drops on days 2-7, the invoice shows the averaged incremental cost rather than a single large overage line.

devin: Implementation note for integrators: pools are per-org by default, but you can attach them to specific routes via route config: 
```
route_config:
  route: /api/v1/generator
  billing:
    pool: mobile-burst
    fallback: metered
```

ops-bot: Deploy: billing-service v3.8.0 will enable pool primitives. Scheduled rollout: 03:00 UTC Friday -> region canary then global. Post-deploy script will migrate pending credit adjustments.

lisa: Customer-facing messaging: we have an opt-in announcement scheduled for Tuesday. Legal reviewed T&Cs for prepay pools; see doc in #legal for exceptions.

patrick: Refund policy: unused prepaid balance can be refunded with 30-day notice; 2% processing fee applies for refunds under $100.

maya: Free-tier impact: free credits (promo/free trial) cannot be applied to prepaid pools. Customers keep their free credits until they consume them via metered routes. We’ll include this in the FAQ.

devin: Metrics to watch in Console: pool balance, burn-rate (tokens/sec), per-route smoothing delta. We’ll add an alert template for unusual burn-rate spikes.

patrick: Billing API changes: new endpoints: 
- POST /billing/pools
- GET /billing/pools/{id}/balance
- POST /billing/pools/{id}/topup
(see internal API doc)

maya: Ops checklist for rollout:
- Canaries: enable in two test orgs
- Monitor: invoice deltas, payment failures
- Support: one-pager for CS + canned responses

lisa: CS one-pager draft is here: <https://redwood.internal/notes/cs-prepay-pools|cs-prepay-pools>. Please comment by EOD Monday.

devin: Q from eng: what about rate limiting? Pools do not bypass rate limits. Rate limits still enforced per-route. Pools only affect billing.

maya: Q from partner team: can partners resell pools? Not in initial launch. We’ll revisit for Partner Marketplace v1.

patrick: Internal accounting: we’ll recognize revenue at time of prepay, then run monthly amortization where required (revenue team to confirm GA treatment).

lisa: Legal flagged: need to show clear pool-to-route mapping in invoices. Engineering: add route label to invoice line items.

maya: Launch timeline recap: Friday deploy, Tuesday public blog + Console flag, next Monday GA.

devin: Any objections?

patrick: none from finance.

lisa: none from CS.

maya: Great — thanks all. Please add any final comments to the doc or ping me. :thumbsup:
